paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God cares about what's in the heart, not just what shows on the outside. Paul talks to the one who calls himself a Jew, who relies on the law and is convinced he's a guide for the blind (Romans 2:17, 19). Then he turns the questions around: "you, then, who teach others, do you not teach yourself?" (Romans 2:21). Knowing the right thing and saying the right thing is not the same as doing it.

Now, I'm not here to point a finger, because my mustache has been in plenty of dough. Paul says circumcision has value if you observe the law, but if you break the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision (Romans 2:25). The sign on the outside can't stand in for a life that lines up with it. And Paul says what that mismatch does: God's name is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you (Romans 2:24).

So what counts? Paul says "a man is a Jew because he is one inwardly, and circumcision is a matter of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the written code" (Romans 2:29). That means a label, a title or a habit you can show off will never be enough. God is after a heart the Spirit has changed. And "such a man's praise does not come from men, but from God" (Romans 2:29), so you can stop performing for the crowd, baker, and live for the One who sees the heart.
